key_insight: A spectral interface-evolution model captures fluid-fluid displacement in rough fractures beyond the quasistatic limit and shows that viscosity changes relaxation dynamics without changing the total dissipated energy.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, multiscale prediction of hysteresis and dissipation in porous and fractured media, useful for upscaling flow behavior in subsurface and industrial transport systems.
method: Spectral computational approach for interface evolution and energy dissipation
Validated against CFD simulations and experiments
Applied to a single-defect fracture and random roughness cases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation via CFD and experiments, plus computational tests showing nontrivial dynamics over many orders of magnitude in time.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated on a model imperfect Hele-Shaw cell, so extension to more complex real fractures may require additional geometric and physical modeling.
paper_title: Dynamics of fluid-fluid displacements in a model rough fracture beyond the quasistatic limit: A spectral approach
